text:
Alex: Handoff — I'm out at 17:00 PT. Quick clarification request before I go: who is the owner for network-level throttles vs model fallback behavior? Also what's our working definition of an 'incident' vs a 'degraded' state? Leaving a few notes below so next oncall has context.

Marina: Short version: Runtime owns model-level behavior (model fallback variants, quantization flags, batching/caching config, KV cache correctness). SRE owns infra-level stuff (network, node/GPU availability, LB misconfig, k8s/driver failures). If it's an infrastructure outage or region-wide SLO breach -> SRE leads. If it's model quality/regression or an internal model-serving bug -> Runtime leads. :thumbsup:

Sam: Where does cache warmup / warming strategy live? If warmup spikes tokens/cost but reduces p90 latency later, who signs off?

Marina: Warmup strategy is proposed/owned by Runtime (they control the feature flags and rollout gates). But if warmup meaningfully impacts cluster capacity or causes infra alerts, SRE is looped in per the runbook. For emergency rollbacks: SRE can revert infra autoscaling or route traffic; Runtime can flip model-serving flags.

Devin: Can we make the escalation path explicit so handoffs are less fuzzy? Proposed minimal path that we can paste into the top of the handoff doc: 

```
1) Pager fires -> infra oncall (SRE) investigates.
2) If investigation points to model quality/regression or model-serving code, infra oncall pings #runtime-oncall and tags runtime lead.
3) If it's clear model-only degradation (not infra), runtime oncall takes lead and updates incident channel.
4) If cross-cutting (both infra + model) -> SRE creates incident and assigns both runtime + infra responders.
5) Customer-facing correctness regressions (bad outputs) = treat as INCIDENT and page both sides immediately.
```

Devin: Also recommend adding a short decision tree to the runbook (I'll draft) and put it at top-level so handoffs can point to it.

oncall-bot: Reminder — rotation: Alex -> Sam at 17:00 PT (auto-reminder).

Alex: FYI — I'm running a quantization rollout in staging and a canary in eu-west tonight. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/834 — if you see a sudden spike in hallucinations or failure to load KV cache, treat customer-facing regressions as incidents. Runtime will monitor eval dashboards but flag to infra if we see node OOMs or degraded autoscaling behavior.

Sam: Got it, I'll pick this up. Adding the PR and this thread to my handoff checklist.

Marina: I'll update the central runbook with the snippet Devin posted and add a short paragraph clarifying "what counts as an incident" (SLO breach, customer correctness regression, P0 availability loss). Will ping when done.

Alex: Thanks all — leaving the workspace in good shape, ping me if you hit anything odd before 17:00. :rocket:
